analysis_notes.structural_note: Torah #241 is an unusually short, eitza-dominant teaching. The entire seven-sentence text is built around a single causal mechanism (human vengeance displaces divine judgment → tzaddik exploits this to protect Israel) with very few bechina equivalences. The dominant relationship type in this Torah is eitza (cause-effect), not bechina (parallel nature). The only unambiguous bechina cluster is the Package 1 family (divine judgment under its three names). Package 2 rests on a structural/narrative identification rather than explicit bechina language.
analysis_notes.good_evil_mirror: Package 2 (the tzaddik — good) is the positive responder to Package 1 (divine judgment — evil). The tzaddik uses the evil force's own logic (the preference to yield to a vengeful human) to redirect and ultimately dissolve it through mercy. This is a functional mirror in the eitza dimension: the good actor operates by understanding and exploiting the evil force's nature. The bechina mirror is incomplete — there is no explicit 'evil version of the tzaddik' node in this Torah.
